title: AlignSep: Temporally-Aligned Video-Queried Sound Separation with Flow Matching
claim: Prior methods use only semantic cues and fail to separate same-category sources; ours uses temporal alignment to separate them correctly.
layout: 2 halves split by dashed line; left setup, right stacked prior vs ours waveforms
description: The figure has two halves separated by a vertical dashed line. On the left, a film-strip frame labeled On-Screen shows an orange dog and a blue standing person. Beside it, labeled Off-Screen, are a gray van and a green dog. Below is a Mixed Audio waveform in blue, orange, gray and green, with a small inset of the four source icons. On the right, two stacked waveform panels give the outputs. The top one is titled Semantically-Aligned VQSS in red with a red X. Its waveform still contains green off-screen dog energy mixed in with the blue and orange. The bottom one is titled Temporally-Aligned VQSS (ours) in green with a green check. Its waveform contains only the on-screen blue and orange sources. Color coding links each icon to its waveform. The eye goes first to the red and green titles.
caption: Comparison of different video-queried sound separation methods. Traditional category-based methods rely solely on semantic information, struggling to distinguish same-source sounds across on/off-screen regions (e.g., multiple dogs barking). In contrast, our proposed AlignSep can capture audiovisual consistency, enabling precise separation of on/off-screen sounds.
abstract: Video Query Sound Separation (VQSS) aims to isolate target sounds conditioned on visual queries while suppressing off-screen interference—a task central to audiovisual understanding. However, existing methods often fail under conditions of homogeneous interference and overlapping soundtracks, due to limited temporal modeling and weak audiovisual alignment. We propose \textbf{AlignSep}, the first generative VQSS model based on flow matching, designed to address common issues such as spectral holes and incomplete separation. To better capture cross-modal correspondence, we introduce a series of temporal consistency mechanisms that guide the vector field estimator toward learning robust audiovisual alignment, enabling accurate and resilient separation in complex scenes. As a \textit{multi-conditioned generation} task, VQSS presents unique challenges that differ fundamentally from traditional flow matching setups. We provide an in-depth analysis of these differences and their implications for generative modeling. To systematically evaluate performance under realistic and difficult conditions, we further construct \textbf{VGGSound-Hard}, a challenging benchmark composed entirely of separation cases with homogeneous interference and strong reliance on temporal visual cues. Extensive experiments across multiple benchmarks demonstrate that AlignSep achieves state-of-the-art performance both quantitatively and perceptually, validating its practical value for real-world applications. More results and audio examples are available at: \url{https://AlignSep.github.io}.
